sourceVariantTitle: How Do We Keep an Eye on Asteroids?
scoreRule: One point per correct answer; ten points maximum. Provisional local result only.
description: Original ten-question B1 English Reading assessment draft; teacher content audit is still required.

tabs.title: Understanding
tabs.description: Understand the central ideas and the people.

tabs.title: Using What You Read
tabs.description: Apply the idea in a new situation.

questions.q: Why do scientists study asteroids as objects from the distant past?
choices: They can reveal the exact date Earth will stop orbiting the Sun.
They always contain materials that do not exist on Earth.
They can provide clues to the early solar system.
They all have identical shapes after travelling for billions of years.
questions.explanation: The article distinguishes careful measurement and controlled experiments from claims that every possible asteroid hazard can be prevented.

questions.q: Why does a single photograph give only limited information about an asteroid's future path?
choices: A photograph can show only the colour of the object.
More observations are needed to calculate its orbit with confidence.
Asteroids stop moving when telescopes cannot see them.
One photograph is enough only when the object is very large.
questions.explanation: The article distinguishes careful measurement and controlled experiments from claims that every possible asteroid hazard can be prevented.

questions.q: How should a reader understand DART's success in the article?
choices: The spacecraft was sent to stop an asteroid already approaching Earth.
It proved that a single impact would destroy any future asteroid.
It prevented Dimorphos from travelling around the Sun.
It was a useful preparation experiment, not the end of every possible threat.
questions.explanation: The article distinguishes careful measurement and controlled experiments from claims that every possible asteroid hazard can be prevented.

questions.q: Why did flying glass cause many injuries in Chelyabinsk?
choices: The shock wave broke windows even though the rock exploded high above the ground.
People stood too close to a newly formed crater.
The meteorite landed directly inside the city's hospitals.
Scientists had warned everyone to watch through open windows.
questions.explanation: The article distinguishes careful measurement and controlled experiments from claims that every possible asteroid hazard can be prevented.

questions.q: What makes the direction from which the Chelyabinsk rock arrived important?
choices: The object came from the direction of Jupiter's asteroid belt.
A rock arriving near the Sun cannot cause damage.
Bright sunlight can make small incoming objects hard to detect.
Scientists could only use computers during the day.
questions.explanation: The article distinguishes careful measurement and controlled experiments from claims that every possible asteroid hazard can be prevented.

questions.q: What does the article suggest about an early warning of a real impact risk?
choices: It could provide essential time for decisions and possible action.
It would remove the need for any international cooperation.
It would guarantee that a spacecraft could stop every impact.
It would show that observing the sky is no longer necessary.
questions.explanation: The article distinguishes careful measurement and controlled experiments from claims that every possible asteroid hazard can be prevented.

questions.q: Why does the author mention exaggerated headlines near the end?
choices: Headlines are more reliable than telescope measurements.
Clear explanations help the public distinguish careful preparation from panic.
Asteroid warnings are useful only when they make people frightened.
The writer wants all news about space to disappear.
questions.explanation: The article distinguishes careful measurement and controlled experiments from claims that every possible asteroid hazard can be prevented.

questions.q: A telescope team gets a new orbit estimate that differs from last week's result. What should they do?
choices: Use the original estimate because it was published first.
Assume the asteroid changed its orbit deliberately.
Stop collecting data until the result looks less alarming.
Compare further observations and explain how the estimate changed.
questions.explanation: The article distinguishes careful measurement and controlled experiments from claims that every possible asteroid hazard can be prevented.

questions.q: A pupil says, 'DART changed an orbit, so we no longer need to look for asteroids.' What is the best response?
choices: A spacecraft can always find and stop a threat without telescope data.
Finding a possible danger early remains necessary before anyone can respond.
Only the largest asteroids should ever be observed.
Scientists should spend all their time repeating the same impact experiment.
questions.explanation: The article distinguishes careful measurement and controlled experiments from claims that every possible asteroid hazard can be prevented.

questions.q: Which school newspaper headline would be most consistent with the article's message?
choices: A close pass proves that a collision will follow soon.
Every asteroid seen near Earth is a new emergency.
There is no reason to continue observing the sky.
Asteroid monitoring improves preparation although major impacts are rare.
questions.explanation: The article distinguishes careful measurement and controlled experiments from claims that every possible asteroid hazard can be prevented.
